memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Moses and Eleazar the priest received from them the gold—all the crafted articles. All the gold from the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds that Moses and Eleazar presented as a gift to the Lord was 16,750 shekels. Each soldier had taken plunder for himself. Moses and Eleazar the priest accepted the gold from the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the Lord. - Num 31:51-54 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with the gold being brought into the tent of meeting as a memorial before the Lord. It was not spent, not hoarded, not put on display for human admiration. It was placed in God's presence as a lasting reminder — a memorial that God had given the victory and that His people had responded with grateful worship.

Memorials matter. God's people are prone to forget, and so throughout Scripture He gives His people ways to remember His faithfulness. Stones, feasts, offerings, songs — all of them saying: do not forget what the Lord has done. When we forget His past mercies, we grow anxious about the present and fearful about the future. Remembering steadies our faith.

We have our own memorial, given by Jesus Himself. On the night before He died, He gave us the Lord's Supper and said, "Do this in remembrance of me" (Luke 22:19). The bread and the cup are our memorial before God — not gold from a battlefield, but signs of the far greater victory Christ won at the cross. Every time we take them, we remember that our deliverance is finished and secure.

So let this chapter, hard and heavy in places, end on a note of remembrance. Whatever we have passed through, God has been faithful. Build your memorials. Do not forget His works. And let your remembering lead you, again and again, to worship.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you actively remember God's faithfulness in your life?
2. What "memorials" could you build to help you not forget His mercies?
3. How does the Lord's Supper help you remember Christ's finished victory?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, help me never to forget what You have done. Thank You for the greater victory of the cross, and for the memorial of the Lord's table. Keep my heart worshipful and remembering. Amen.
